title: Heidelberger Study on lower Limb Protection
summary:
Diabetic sensorimotor polyneuropathy (DSPN) is a common complication of diabetes and the leading cause of non-traumatic lower limb amputations. Due to its frequent association with peripheral arterial occlusive disease (PAD), caused by diabetes-related vascular changes, the risk of amputation is significantly increased in these patients. Additionally, long-standing diabetes often leads to early-onset sarcopenia (muscle wasting), which further increases morbidity and mortality in affected individuals.

In a planned study, tissue samples from amputated limbs of patients with PAD or diabetic neuropathy who require amputation will be analyzed. The aim is to better understand the underlying causes and mechanisms of these changes. Tissue samples from adipose tissue, skeletal muscle, nerves, blood vessels, and bone will be examined using advanced methods such as electron microscopy, pathological analyses, and immunohistochemical staining.

Prior to surgery, patients will be categorized into groups based on their medical history, comorbidities, and medication to distinguish between those with and without diabetic neuropathy. The goal of the study is to gain a deeper understanding of the histological and molecular changes in these tissues, thereby contributing to the elucidation of the underlying disease processes.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Participants with a defined indication for amputation
Ability to provide informed consent, understand the explanations about the study, and follow instructions
Individuals with manifest type 1 or type 2 diabetes mellitus, with a confirmed diagnosis according to the 2011 DDG criteria (i.e., HbA1c ≥ 6.5% excluding factors that could distort HbA1c results, ≥ 200 mg/dl 2-hour value during an oral glucose tolerance test (oGTT), pathological fasting glucose ≥ 126 mg/dl, or at least two pathological random glucose readings of ≥ 200 mg/dl), or
Participants without diabetes or any glucose metabolism disorder, as confirmed by an oral glucose tolerance test (oGTT) according to the 2011 DDG criteria: fasting venous plasma glucose < 100 mg/dl and 2-hour venous plasma glucose < 140 mg/dl, or
Individuals with prediabetes, characterized by impaired fasting glucose between 100 mg/dl and 125 mg/dl or impaired glucose tolerance with a 2-hour oGTT value between 140-199 mg/dl (venous), or HbA1c levels between 5.7% and 6.4%.
Exclusion criteria:
HbA1c >10%
Secondary causes of diabetes mellitus
Other causes of peripheral polyneuropathy
Severe autoimmune diseases
Immunomodulating therapy
Known severe psychiatric illnesses requiring treatment (e.g., personality disorders, schizophrenia, depression)
Known dependency on alcohol or other drugs
Known malignant cancer diagnosis within the past 5 years
Current participation in another interventional study

Exclusion criteria for MRI:
Pacemaker / ICD
Metallic and magnetic implants (e.g., mechanical heart valves, joint prostheses, vascular clips, middle or inner ear implants, recent dental implants, penile implants)
Waist circumference >135 cm
Claustrophobia
Known allergy to MRI contrast agents
GFR (CKD-EPI) < 60 ml/min/1.73 m²

Exclusion criteria for BIA measurement:
Pacemaker / ICD
